problem: Existing EQA benchmarks focus on household scenes with short phrasal answers. They ignore industrial settings, safety-critical hazards, human workers, and evaluation of the reasoning behind an answer.
motivation: Real-world warehouse deployment requires agents that recognise safety hazards and reason about them, but collecting real warehouse data is costly and raises privacy, safety and liability concerns. Simulation in Isaac Sim gives controllable, diverse, hazard-rich scenes with animated humans, so agent readiness can be measured safely.
key_idea: Build IndustryEQA, an episodic-memory EQA benchmark of Isaac Sim warehouse videos with 1,344 QA pairs in six categories (two safety, four perception), each with a direct answer and a reasoning answer, scored by an LLM judge.
insight: Blind LLMs score far below video-capable VLLMs (about 33-44% direct vs about 50-70%), so the questions really need visual grounding. Reasoning scores are almost always below direct scores, and temporal understanding is the hardest category, so justification and temporal reasoning remain open problems. Increasing the number of sampled frames (5 to 50) consistently helps with diminishing returns, and the two LLM judges show similar trends.
method: Simulation and scenes: 4 experts build 60 small and 16 large warehouse layouts in Isaac Sim from industrial assets (workers, forklifts, racks, signage). Hazards are inspired by OSHA 'Hazards and Solutions' guidance, e.g. blocked exits, unsecured ladders, missing fire extinguishers, forklift-human lane sharing.

Video capture: an egocentric camera on a ROS Carter robot (30 fps, 1080P, z=1) is teleoperated by keyboard to cover the whole warehouse. One video per scenario is recorded, giving 76 videos (mean 85.2 s small, 240 s large).

QA generation: Gemini 2.5 Pro takes each video and a safety-focused prompt and produces QA pairs across six categories (at least 50% safety). Each pair has a direct answer and a one-sentence reasoning answer, and the first pass gave over 3,000 pairs.

QA transformation and LLM refinement: Yes/No questions are turned into open-ended or multiple-choice ones by Gemini 2.5 Pro, o4-mini, o4-mini-high and o3. An LLM pass then checks video dependence, type consistency and answer correctness, and flags pairs to retain or remove.
Human filtering: trained experts verify correctness, remove ambiguity, increase difficulty and validate categories, leaving 971 small-warehouse and 373 large-warehouse QA pairs.

Evaluation: baselines are Blind LLMs, Multi-Frame VLLMs (30 frames small, 40 large) and Video VLLMs, all zero-shot via OpenRouter. An LLM judge (GPT-4o-mini, also Gemini-2.0-Flash) gives a 1-5 score, normalised as C=(σ-1)/4·100, reported separately for Direct Score and Reasoning Score.

setting.backbone: Zero-shot baselines: blind LLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini-2.0-Flash, DeepSeek-R1/V3), multi-frame VLLMs (LLaMA-4-Scout, Qwen2.5-VL-72B, InternVL2.5-78B, Claude-3.5-Haiku, GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, o4-mini), video VLLMs (Gemini-2.0-Flash, Gemini-2.5-Flash), all frozen
setting.training_data: none (benchmark paper; all models evaluated zero-shot)
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB episodic-memory video (1080P, 30 fps), sampled to 30/40 frames for multi-frame models
setting.action_space: none (passive episodic-memory QA; video collected by manual keyboard teleoperation)

numbers_note: IndustryEQA is not among the canonical benchmarks, and the paper reports baseline results only. It has no own-method rows, so no numbers are extracted. Per-category results and the frame-count and judge ablations appear only in figures.
results: o4-mini is the best multi-frame VLLM (Direct 69.67 small, Reasoning 67.71 small), and Gemini-2.5-Flash video is the best on large warehouses (Direct 70.24), followed by GPT-4.1. Blind LLMs reach only about 33-44% direct, and reasoning scores are generally lower than direct scores. Attribute recognition is the easiest category and temporal understanding the hardest.
limitations: The asset library is limited: few overhead-walkway variants, incomplete container labels and chemical hazard markings, so some non-OSHA-violation scenarios cannot be recreated.
Scenes are largely static, with conservative motion of humans and vehicles, no event-driven, extreme or time-of-day dynamics, no audio, and only one video per scenario.

The setting is passive episodic-memory QA scored by an LLM judge, and the judge is lenient in different ways depending on the model. Questions were generated with Gemini 2.5 Pro (a possible bias), and there is no active exploration, no real-world validation, and no training or fine-tuning baselines.
